rules.subject: Scope test - definition of 'health care services'

rules.subject: THRESHOLD RULE - hospital room charges above INR 5,000 per day (non-ICU) fall out of the healthcare exemption
rules.item_or_service: Hospital room charges, EXCLUDING ICU / CCU / ICCU / NICU
rules.item_classification: Heading 9993 as amended by proviso; taxed under the applicable rate entry for heading 9993
rules.rule_statement: The healthcare-services exemption does NOT apply to a room supplied by a clinical establishment, other than an ICU / CCU / ICCU / NICU, where the room charges exceed INR 5,000 per day, to a person receiving healthcare services.
rules.operational_rule: COMPUTE room_charge_per_day = total_room_charge_for_the_admission / number_of_chargeable_days (or use the invoice's daily room rate where stated). IF room category is NOT ICU/CCU/ICCU/NICU AND room_charge_per_day > INR 5000 THEN the exemption in Sl. No. 74 does NOT apply to that room supply and GST becomes payable on the taxable value of that room supply at the rate applicable to heading 9993 as in force on the invoice date (determine from the rate notification in force on that date - DO NOT assume a rate). IF room_charge_per_day <= INR 5000 THEN the room charge remains part of the exempt healthcare service (GST = Nil). CRITICAL: this is a TAX TREATMENT threshold, not a price cap. A hospital is NOT prohibited from charging more than INR 5,000/day; charging more simply moves that room supply out of the exemption.

conditions: Supplier is a clinical establishment
Room is NOT ICU / CCU / ICCU / NICU
Room charges exceed INR 5,000 per day
Recipient is a person receiving healthcare services

price_control.notes: NO PRICE CONTROL WHATSOEVER. This INR 5,000 figure is purely a GST taxability threshold. It does NOT mean a hospital may not charge more than INR 5,000/day for a room. Do not report this as a price violation.

excluded_items: ICU
CCU
ICCU
NICU
Neo-natal Intensive Care Unit
exceptions: Room charges at or below INR 5,000 per day remain exempt (this side of the threshold is governed by GST-IN-HC-001)

rules.subject: Cashless discharge authorization within three hours - delay charge borne by the insurer
rules.item_or_service: Final discharge authorization
rules.rule_statement: Insurer shall grant final authorization within three hours of the receipt of discharge authorization request from the hospital. In no case, the policyholder shall be made to wait to be discharged from the Hospital. If there is any delay beyond three hours, the additional amount if any charged by the hospital shall be borne by the insurer from shareholder's fund.
rules.operational_rule: IF a discharge-delay charge appears on the bill as a patient-payable item (for example 'waiting charges', 'delay charges', 'extended stay charges' levied after an authorization delay) THEN flag as an INSURER_OBLIGATION finding: under IRDAI's 2024 Master Circular the additional amount charged by the hospital for a delay beyond three hours is to be borne by the INSURER from its shareholder's fund, not passed to the policyholder. This is one of the few rules in the database where a cost is placed on the insurer rather than the hospital. Escalate to the insurer / IRDDAI grievance channel.

price_control.who_is_bound: The INSURER - it must absorb the delay charge from shareholder's fund.
price_control.notes: Process and cost-allocation obligation. Not a cap on the hospital's charge.

rules.subject: Pre-existing disease (PED) look-back window - parameterize, do not hard-code
rules.item_or_service: Pre-existing disease exclusion
rules.rule_statement: Pre-Existing Disease (PED) means any condition, ailment, injury or disease that is diagnosed by a physician within the look-back window prior to the effective date of the policy, or for which medical advice or treatment was recommended by or received from a physician within that window.

rules.subject: Internal consistency check - quantity x rate must equal the billed line amount, and the invoice GST arithmetic must reconcile
rules.item_or_service: Any billed line and any GST invoice
rules.rule_statement: A bill line is internally inconsistent if billed_amount != quantity x unit_price. An invoice is internally inconsistent if taxable_value x rate != tax_amount, or if the sum of line amounts plus tax does not equal the invoice total.
rules.operational_rule: PERFORM BEFORE ANY LEGAL CHECK - arithmetic errors are independent of law and are the highest-confidence, lowest-false-positive findings. (1) For each line: expected = quantity x unit_price; if abs(expected - billed_amount) > tolerance THEN flag 'ARITHMETIC ERROR on line'. (2) For the invoice: for each GST slab, verify taxable_value x rate = tax_amount; verify line_total_sum + tax_total = invoice_total; verify that the GST amount shown equals the GST amount implied by the rate applied under the applicable GST rule for that line. NOTE: (3) is a control on internal consistency, NOT proof that the correct RATE was applied - the rate correctness check is governed by GST-IN-HC-001 through GST-IN-HC-014.

conditions: Determines the rate actually applied on the invoice so it can be compared against the applicable rule

price_control.notes: Mathematical consistency control. No legal source is required because the rule is arithmetic, not legal.

exceptions: Apply a documented tolerance (for example absolute INR 1 plus a rounding allowance) to avoid rounding false positives

rules.subject: Duplicate charge control - identical service line appearing more than once
rules.item_or_service: Any billed service or item
rules.rule_statement: A duplicate charge exists where the same service or item appears more than once on a bill without supporting evidence justifying the repetition.
rules.operational_rule: STEP 1: normalise each bill line description (lowercase, strip punctuation, expand common abbreviations, strip quantities and dates). STEP 2: group lines by normalised description. STEP 3: for each group with count > 1, test the documented legitimate-repetition whitelist before raising a finding: (a) qty-driven items where billed quantity equals the expected clinical frequency for the documented length of stay; (b) daily items where quantity equals the number of chargeable days; (c) items under a per-day medical management package. STEP 4: if no whitelist reason applies, flag 'POTENTIALLY DUPLICATED' - never 'DUPLICATE'. Do not auto-reject: emit the finding with the grouped line numbers and the computed duplicate value so a human can adjudicate.

rules.subject: Clinical inconsistency must be labelled as a POTENTIAL inconsistency, never a confirmed medical error
rules.item_or_service: Any treatment, drug, or investigation line
rules.rule_statement: A treatment line may be flagged as potentially clinically inconsistent with an official clinical guideline, but such a flag must never be presented as a confirmed medical error.
rules.operational_rule: ALLOWED OUTPUT VALUES ARE ONLY: POTENTIALLY_CLINICALLY_INCONSISTENT or REQUIRES_CLINICAL_REVIEW. NEVER output CONFIRMED_MEDICAL_ERROR. Required evidence fields for any clinical flag: the guideline or protocol relied on (must be an official MoHFW / NHA / CGHS / professional-body source), the specific billed line, and the reason for the mismatch. Known high-signal patterns that MAY be flagged as potential inconsistencies: investigations not consistent with the documented provisional diagnosis; a drug whose dose or route is inconsistent with the documented diagnosis; a procedure billed without the corresponding documented investigation or clinical note. Where an official Standard Treatment Guideline was not located in this database, emit REQUIRES_CLINICAL_REVIEW with INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rather than asserting a clinical rule.
